value: Welles's memorandum of conversation: the Anglo-Italian Agreement signed 16 Apr 1938, presented as settling the two governments' differences
source: FRUS 1938 vol. I doc. 90 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1938v01/d90); Anglo-Italian Agreement and protocol of Rome 16 April 1938
rule: The false member: the Claude replay reader reads the post-Ethiopia estrangement as ended by the signed agreement (reports/replay_ww2_frus_claude, proposal 1938Q2-013). The delegated review rejected the proposal (the agreement signed but expressly not in force, the conquest of Ethiopia unrecognised; review_sample.csv).

value: Bullitt reports Chamberlain 'extremely proud of his agreement with Italy' and 'unquestionably a change in Italy's attitude toward France'
rule: The false member: read false by both blind replay readers (Claude proposal 1938Q2-041; DeepSeek proposal 1938Q2-035; reports/replay_ww2_frus_claude/metrics_claude.md quotes it as the replay's level at 1938Q2). The delegated review rejected the Claude proposal (no agreement in force; Daladier's scepticism reported alongside; review_sample.csv).

value: France's decision to recognise the Italian Empire and send an ambassador to Rome
rule: The false member: a Western power formally settling the Ethiopian question (Claude proposal 1938Q4-007), accepted by the delegated review (review_sample.csv).

value: Britain recognises Italian sovereignty over Ethiopia and the Anglo-Italian Agreement is put into force by a declaration signed in Rome on 16 Nov 1938
rule: The false member: read false by both blind replay readers (Claude proposal 1938Q4-039, accepted by the delegated review, review_sample.csv; DeepSeek proposal 1938Q4-056).

value: Bullitt, at the May crisis: 'even though England were to take the course outlined in the British Government's memorandum, Germany would not hesitate to make war any more than she had hesitated in 1914'
rule: The will_fight member: the DeepSeek replay reader reads Berlin as expecting the West to fight (proposal 1938Q2-060; replayed will_fight at 1938Q2, reports/replay_ww2_frus_deepseek/metrics_deepseek.md). Not in the Claude review sample.

value: Kennedy reports Hitler's reply to Chamberlain's warning: 'Hitler said he was perfectly willing to take on a world war'
rule: The will_fight member: the Claude replay reader reads it as Hitler accepting war with Britain and France (proposal 1938Q3-058; replayed will_fight at 1938Q3 and 1938Q4, reports/replay_ww2_frus_claude/metrics_claude.md). The delegated review rejected it (a counter-threat in a negotiation, not a German record of belief; review_sample.csv).

value: USSR accept_pact: the German-Soviet non-aggression pact of 23 Aug 1939, whose effect in v1 is oil_GER := secured
source: Treaty of Non-Aggression between Germany and the USSR, Moscow, 23 August 1939 (Nazi-Soviet Relations 1939-1941); data/ww2/realized_moves_v1.csv tick 14 (1939Q3); models/ww2/v1.py USSR action accept_pact
rule: The secured member on v1's own clock (the snapshot convention, docs/ambiguous_levels.md section 3): the realized accept_pact of 1939Q3 sets oil_GER secured, so the model's value is one of the members. The German-Soviet credit agreement of 19 Aug 1939 is not used as a source (owner's decision 5c).

value: German-Soviet Commercial Agreement: Soviet oil and grain deliveries against German manufactures
source: German-Soviet Commercial Agreement, Moscow, 11 February 1940 (DGFP series D); Tooze 2006, The Wages of Destruction (chapter not verified)
rule: The secured member: the record's later deliveries, dated after the window (the canonical snapshots date secured from them, at 1940Q1). Read here as the record's confirmation that the pact's economic side was carried out, which the model's clock anticipates at the pact; the dependent member keeps the delivery date. For the historian.
